story: Little Things That Made Amiga Great
text: The Amiga has a very impressive demoscene... Two Amiga demos that I like from The Black Lotus (TBL): - Eon (2019): [LINK] (4:16 is my favorite part) - Starstruck (2006): [VIDEO]

I've owned one, though i never programmed for it. But from what i know, i guess the answer is that the amiga is very close to a modern computer, in that it has specialized chips for graphics and sound (Denise and Paula), making many tasks quite easy, but is still weak enough to force most programs to be relatively simple. At the same time there's also still a very active competitive amiga programming community², making things like these: [LINK] -- [LINK] -- [VIDEO] -- [LINK] -- [LINK] ² [LINK]

story: The demo scene is dying, but that's alright
text: I was just walking down demoscene memory lane yesterday. Some of my favorite demoscene demos were Amiga ones (playlist: [VIDEO] ), which lead me to "The Greatest Video Game Tech Demo Ever," Shadow the Beast: [LINK] That video's great because it breaks down how Psygnosis managed to get 12 layers of parallax scrolling at 50fps and 128 colors on-screen. I never really loved the game as much as (say) Blood Money, but it was an awesome accomplishment in the same way demoscene demos were!
